desc:
In the array nums, nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i: from i you may jump to any index j with i < j ≤ i + nums[i] (and j inside the array). An index with nums[i] = 0 cannot move at all.

Call an index good if you can reach the last index by starting there and jumping zero or more times. The last index is always good. Return the number of good indices.

[2, 3, 1, 1, 4] -> 5
[3, 2, 1, 0, 4] -> 1
[1, 0, 2, 0]    -> 2   (indices 2 and 3)
hints: The classic 'can I reach the end from index 0' question is solved greedily. Here you must answer it for every starting index, so process the array in a smart order.
Go from right to left. An index is good if it can jump onto some index that is already known to be good.
Keep g, the smallest good index found so far. Any good index in the range of i is at least g, so i is good exactly when i + nums[i] ≥ g. Then g becomes i.
editorial: Scan from the right and remember g, the leftmost index known to be good (initially the last index). For an index i to be good it must be able to land on a good index in (i, i + nums[i]]. All good indices to the right are at least g, so if any of them is reachable, then g itself is reachable (it is the closest one and the reach is a contiguous range starting at i + 1). Hence i is good if and only if i + nums[i] ≥ g.

When i is good, set g = i and increase the counter. Indices that are bad leave g unchanged. One right-to-left pass, O(n) time, O(1) space. This is the standard 'jump game' greedy turned into a counting version.
